evidence_items.explanation: The experiments show that language-model-based robotic planning can improve through environmental feedback. This challenges a blanket dismissal of the approach, but does not demonstrate dependable, safe household operation or isolate world comprehension as the decisive cause.

Later work reports improved household planning with additional memory and planning components, while substantial task failures remain. Its benchmark abstracts away physical control and uses a different system, so it cannot settle the claim about the criticized architecture.

unresolved_gaps: No cited evaluation isolates limited world comprehension as a cause that makes dependable robot performance unattainable.
The cited successes do not establish sustained, safe performance across ordinary household environments.
The speaker supplies no criterion for deciding whether added grounding, feedback, or memory changes the kind of system being criticized.
